name: Hong Bang
tagline: French colonial core around the Opera House
description: Hong Bang is the administrative and commercial heart of Hai Phong, built around the ochre Opera House, the flower-lined Tam Bac lake and wide boulevards of French colonial villas. Ground floors hold banks, bakeries, coffee chains and the city's better restaurants. It is where visiting businesspeople and most short-stay foreigners end up.
bestFor: Nomads who want a walkable centre with proper cafes and the widest choice of serviced apartments.
pros: Most walkable district with lakes and shaded boulevards
Best cafe and coworking-friendly coffee shop density
Close to the train station and buses to Ha Long
cons: Motorbike traffic and horns from early morning
Pavements are largely occupied by parked bikes

name: Ngo Quyen
tagline: Busy midtown with the best street food
description: Ngo Quyen stretches east from the centre toward the river port, packed with market streets, banh mi que stalls, seafood restaurants and the Vincom Plaza mall. Newer apartment towers sit alongside old shophouses, so you can get a modern flat without paying colonial-quarter prices. It is where most working Hai Phong residents actually live.
bestFor: Nomads who want good value modern apartments with real Vietnamese street life outside.
pros: Best street food in the city, meals around $2
Modern towers with lifts and reliable fibre
Ten minute ride to the colonial centre
cons: Air quality suffers from port and truck traffic
Almost no English outside the mall

name: Le Chan
tagline: Residential southwest with parks and cheap rent
description: Le Chan covers the southwestern city, a grid of ordinary residential streets, local markets, the Nu Tuong Dai park area and the big Lach Tray stadium. Housing is mostly tube houses and mid-rise blocks aimed at families, and rents drop noticeably compared with the centre. Days are quiet and life runs on local prices.
bestFor: Long-stay nomads who want a quiet family neighbourhood and rents well under the centre.
pros: Clearly cheaper rents than Hong Bang
Quiet residential streets, good for calls
Local markets and gyms without tourist pricing
cons: Few cafes or coworking options nearby
Needs a motorbike, walking distances are long
Streets flood in heavy summer rain

name: Hai An
tagline: New east-side developments near the airport
description: Hai An is the eastern district holding Cat Bi airport and the newest planned developments, with wide new roads, gated compounds and modern serviced apartments. It is spacious and orderly compared with the old centre, and popular with Korean and Japanese staff working at nearby factories. Everything is new, which means good buildings and little atmosphere.
bestFor: Nomads who fly often and want a new, quiet apartment over old-town character.
pros: Newest housing stock with the best internet
Ten minutes to Cat Bi airport
Korean and Japanese restaurants and supermarkets
cons: Aircraft noise on some approach paths
Little street life, you drive everywhere

name: Kien An
tagline: Cheapest option across the Lach Tray river
description: Kien An lies southwest across the Lach Tray river, half small-town and half city, with a hill park, university campuses and low-rise streets of local shops. Rents are the lowest of any district within reach of the centre and food prices match. Expect almost no foreigners and a strongly local daily rhythm.
bestFor: Very budget-conscious nomads happy to trade a river crossing for the lowest rent around.
pros: Lowest rents within reach of the city
Kien An hill park and greener surroundings
Student area keeps food and services cheap
cons: Bridge traffic makes the commute unpredictable
Very limited cafes, gyms or English services
